data.title: Choose the correct answer for each question.
data.description: Common grammar patterns for Vietnamese learners
learningPoints: Focuses on grammar patterns commonly influenced by Vietnamese language structure.
Improves control of adjective forms such as interested vs interesting.
Builds accuracy with articles, plurals, and prepositions.
Strengthens sentence structure for professional and academic communication.
Helps avoid common mistakes in international English contexts.
ESOL B1–B2 and aligns with IELTS 5.5–6.5 and TOEFL iBT 60–94 score ranges.

sections.explain: Adjectives ending in '-ed' describe how a person feels.

words.word: I am very interested in music.
I am very interesting in music.
I very interested in music.

sections.summary: Use articles with singular countable nouns.
sections.explain: Singular countable nouns require an article such as 'a' or 'the'.

words.word: She bought a new laptop yesterday.
She bought new laptop yesterday.
She bought the new laptop yesterday one.

sections.summary: Use plural forms for countable nouns.
sections.explain: Plural nouns require the '-s' ending when referring to more than one.

words.word: Many students study English here.
Many student study English here.
Many students studies English here.

sections.explain: After 'to', the base form of the verb should be used.

words.word: I want to improve my English skills.
I want improve my English skills.
I want to improving my English skills.

sections.summary: Use correct prepositions with common verbs.
sections.explain: The verb 'listen' is followed by the preposition 'to'.

words.word: She listens to music every day.
She listens music every day.
She listen to music every day.

sections.explain: 'There are' is used when referring to plural objects.

words.word: There are many restaurants in this area.
Have many restaurants in this area.
There have many restaurants in this area.

sections.explain: Past actions require past tense verbs such as 'went'.

words.word: We went to the beach last weekend.
We go to the beach last weekend.
We gone to the beach last weekend.

sections.explain: English sentences usually require a form of the verb 'to be'.

words.word: She is very happy today.
She very happy today.
She be very happy today.

sections.summary: Use correct word order in questions.
sections.explain: Questions require auxiliary verbs such as 'do' or 'does'.

words.word: Do you like Vietnamese food?
You like Vietnamese food?
Like you Vietnamese food?

sections.summary: Use natural English expressions instead of translated structures.
sections.explain: English commonly uses 'make a decision' rather than 'do a decision'.

words.word: She made an important decision yesterday.
She did an important decision yesterday.
She make an important decision yesterday.
